title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array, in O(n). Trick: dump into a Set and only start counting from values whose predecessor is missing.

notes: The `if (set.has(x - 1)) continue` guard is what makes this O(n) — without it you'd re-walk runs.
Iterating the Set (not the array) avoids redundant work on duplicates.
Empty input is a base case — best starts at 0 and the loop is a no-op.

questions.q: Why skip values where `x - 1` is also in the set?
options: Those are mid-run; counting only from sequence heads bounds total work to O(n)

questions.explain: Each value is touched at most twice — once as a head, once by the inner while loop.

questions.q: Why iterate the Set instead of the original array?
options: Skip duplicates so the head-check guard does its job

questions.explain: The run 1,2,3,4 has length 4. 100 and 200 are isolated runs of length 1.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the O(n) hash-set solution.

L3.prompt: Write `longestConsecutive(nums)` returning the length of the longest run of consecutive integers, in O(n). Log `longestConsecutive([100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2])`.
hints: Put everything in a Set first.
Only start counting from values whose predecessor is missing.
